sources.title: Print History: Jatindra Kumar Nayak - Print Culture in Odisha
sources.author: Murali Ranganathan
sources.inspection: Web fetch returned403; ordinary Chrome opened full public interview. All questions and answers read in visible accessibility tree, nodes44-109. No login or bypass.
locators: First question: engagement with print, node45
sources.supported_paraphrase: Nayak recalls his father Kashinath managing the Primary Teachers’ Federation press in Puri. As a Ravenshaw student he helped publish Sanskriti and The Ultra and corrected proofs late at presses. He says he began translating Fakir Mohan Senapati’s autobiography at Oxford to counter homesickness. He links translations he enjoyed to their treatment of print culture. At Sikshasandhan, he describes collecting local histories, older textbooks and life writing; he also recalls helping organise a 2014 publishing seminar and introducing a university publishing course.
limits: First-person recollections, not independently observed events.
Autobiography was co-translated; this account of beginning work does not establish sole credit.
